query: What precise complexity, memory bounds, and worst-case runtime guarantees do KD-tree, PCA, Hamming, and hashing alternatives provide for large T and n, and what are acceptable sparse/compression tradeoffs?

response.query: What precise complexity, memory bounds, and worst-case runtime guarantees do KD-tree, PCA, Hamming, and hashing alternatives provide for large T and n, and what are acceptable sparse/compression tradeoffs?
response.answer: KD-tree has O(log T) search complexity, PCA has O(n^3) complexity, Hamming distance has O(n) complexity, and hashing provides O(1) average-case access with trade-offs in memory for collision resolution. Sparse data improves KD-tree and PCA efficiency but may affect Hamming distance and hashing performance.
